newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti stock suspended limit-up in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti stock suspended limit-up in Milan.

text.p: Shares in crisis-struck Italian information technology group Olivetti, which late on Wednesday named a new chief executive, were suspended on Thursday after hitting a 10 percent trading ceiling in pre-bourse price matching.
An fresh attempt to start trade in the stock, which closed on Wednesday at 510 lire per share, will be made at 0850 GMT, the Italian stock market council said.

Olivetti shares, which wallowed at record lows of 465 lire (30 cents) at the start of the week, have repeatedly triggered automatic suspension in volatile activity on the bourse this week by either hitting the 10 percent trading floor or the 10 percent trading ceiling.

Late on Wednesday, in an emergency board meeting, the loss-making group announced its chief executive of three months, Francesco Caio, had resigned and would be replaced by Roberto Colaninno, head of auto components group Sogefi.
Caio's replacement by Colaninno is the latest twist in a succession of tumultuous events since Carlo De Benedetti resigned from the Olivetti board on September 3 after 18 years as group chairman.

Panic selling on the Milan stock exchange has wiped nearly 40 percent off the loss-making company's market capitalisation since De Benedetti's dramatic exit and after doubts were cast over the accuracy of Olivetti's financial accounts. ($ = 1524 Italian Lire)
